title: Migrating to and from OpenAI
summary: This intermediate module teaches you to separate provider-specific details from application behavior so you can plan, test, and reverse a migration involving OpenAI. After completing it, you can build a migration checklist, define an adapter boundary, compare observable behavior, and plan a controlled cutover.
objectives: Identify the application behaviors and provider-specific details that must be recorded before a migration.
Define an adapter boundary that prevents provider-specific request and response details from spreading through an application.
Create behavior-based tests for comparing an existing integration with a replacement.
Plan a staged cutover with explicit acceptance and rollback conditions.
Apply the same migration process when moving either to OpenAI or away from OpenAI.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The changed citation was content/modules/openai-practice/migrating-to-and-from-openai.json, which the update record identifies as an unregistered publisher source that had never been verified. It has been replaced in the source list by OpenAI's official API reference and official OpenAPI specification repository, both using direct HTTPS URLs.

This change affects citation provenance and where learners verify current interface details. Only the source correction and the instruction to consult those official references for live request and response details are affected. The provider migration workflow remains focused on inventory, isolation, testing, cutover, and rollback.
sections.callout: Provider interfaces can change between reviews. Verify current request and response details in the cited official sources before implementing a migration.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate module. It assumes you can read an API reference, inspect structured requests and responses, and understand the purpose of automated tests. It does not assume prior experience migrating between model providers, and it declares no catalogue prerequisites.

A provider migration is not only a request-format conversion. The application may depend on observable behavior such as output structure, failure handling, timing expectations, usage reporting, and the interpretation of instructions. A safe migration records those dependencies before changing the integration.

sections.title: Inventory the existing contract
paragraphs: Begin by documenting what the application sends, what it expects to receive, and what it does when a request fails. Separate required behavior from incidental implementation details. Required behavior might include producing parseable structured output, preserving conversation context, or returning enough information for the application to make its next decision.

Record provider-specific details separately from application requirements. Examples include request shape, response shape, authentication handling, error categories, streaming event interpretation, and usage information. For current OpenAI interface details, use the cited official API reference or official OpenAPI specification repository rather than copying assumptions from an older integration.

Create representative test cases from real application tasks after removing sensitive information. Include ordinary cases, boundary cases, malformed outputs, refusals or unavailable results, interrupted requests, and retryable failures when those situations matter to the application.

sections.title: Isolate provider-specific details
paragraphs: Place a narrow adapter between the application and each provider interface. The application should send an internal request that represents its actual needs. The adapter translates that request into the provider's current format and translates the provider response back into one internal result.

Keep provider-specific response parsing inside the adapter. Code elsewhere in the application should not need to know how a particular provider represents content, status information, usage information, or errors. This boundary reduces the amount of code that must change during either direction of migration.

Do not force unlike behaviors into a misleading common abstraction. If one integration exposes a capability that another does not, represent that difference explicitly and decide whether the application requires it. An adapter should isolate differences, not conceal a missing requirement.

sections.title: Test observable behavior
paragraphs: Compare integrations by the behavior the application needs, not by expecting identical wording. Exact text comparisons are usually too narrow for generated output. Prefer checks such as whether required information is present, whether structured output can be parsed, whether prohibited content is absent, and whether the application can complete its next step.

Run the same representative cases through the existing adapter and the candidate adapter. Record pass or fail results against acceptance criteria chosen before the comparison. Review failures individually because a single aggregate score can hide a severe regression in an important case.

Test failure paths as well as successful paths. Confirm that the adapter converts provider-specific failures into the internal categories the application understands and that retry behavior does not create duplicate side effects.

sections.title: Control the cutover
paragraphs: Define acceptance conditions before routing production work through the candidate adapter. Conditions should cover the behaviors identified in the contract inventory. Also define rollback conditions, the person or process authorized to trigger rollback, and the evidence that will be retained for diagnosis.

Use a staged cutover when the application permits it. Begin with controlled test traffic, then a limited portion of eligible work, and expand only after reviewing the agreed evidence. Keep the previous adapter available until the rollback period ends and the replacement has satisfied the acceptance conditions.

A migration away from OpenAI uses the same sequence as a migration to OpenAI: inventory the current contract, isolate provider details, implement the candidate adapter, compare behavior, stage the cutover, and preserve a rollback path. The direction changes which adapter is current and which is the candidate, but it does not remove the need for evidence.

sections.title: Build the migration checklist
paragraphs: Your checklist should identify the application requirements, current provider-specific assumptions, representative test cases, adapter translation rules, acceptance conditions, rollback conditions, and the official references used to verify interface details.

After completing this module, you can turn an integration that is coupled to one provider into a documented migration plan. You can identify what must remain stable, confine provider differences to an adapter, evaluate a candidate using application-level evidence, and change traffic without discarding the previous path prematurely.

questions.prompt: What should happen before provider-specific integration code is changed?
choices: Document the application's required behavior and current provider-specific assumptions.
Remove the existing adapter so the application can call the candidate directly.
Route all production work through the candidate integration.
Require generated responses from both providers to use identical wording.
questions.explanation: The module directs you to inventory required application behavior and provider-specific dependencies before changing the integration.

questions.prompt: Where should provider-specific request translation and response parsing be kept?
choices: In every application component that uses generated output.
Only in the production traffic router.
questions.explanation: A narrow adapter contains provider-specific translation and parsing so the rest of the application can use one internal contract.

questions.prompt: Which comparison best evaluates a migration involving generated output?
choices: Check whether every response uses exactly the same words.
Check only whether each request completed without an error.
Check whether each integration satisfies predefined application-level requirements.
Check whether the candidate adapter contains fewer lines of code.
questions.explanation: The module recommends predefined behavior checks, such as parseability and required information, rather than exact wording.

questions.prompt: What must be defined before a staged production cutover?
choices: A requirement to delete the previous adapter immediately.
A promise that no provider interface will change.
A rule that only successful requests are tested.
questions.explanation: The cutover section requires explicit acceptance and rollback conditions before production work is moved.
